clinician.final_diagnosis: pubic symphysis disjunction syndrome following a dystocic delivery
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old primigravida presented on day 1 postpartum with acute pubic pain and increased abdomino-pelvic sensitivity after delivering a 4400g male newborn. Pelvic X-ray showed a pubic disjunction, which was further confirmed by abdomino-pelvic CT as a 3 cm pubic symphysis disjunction without fracture, soft tissue infiltration, and normal sacroiliac/coxo-femoral joints. Therapeutic management included unloading, preventive anti-coagulation, and analgesics. The patient experienced a favorable evolution with no painful recurrence and no symphysial sensitivity at the 15-day control.
